description: Retired Army General and former CIA Director David Petraeus says President Trump’s stated goals in Iran are “very achievable” as airstrikes degrade Tehran’s air defenses, missile stockpiles and drone capabilities. Petraeus also calls it “imperative” for the U.S. to rebuild its military industrial complex and dramatically increase weapons production to prepare for future wars. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of  Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Petraeus Says Iran Objectives ‘Very Achievable’ From the Air

description: Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL) shares her reaction to the ongoing conflict in the Mideast. Wasserman Schultz says she is "really concerned" about depleting munitions as a result of US strikes and would support an emergency supplemental funding request. The Congresswoman also cited concerns about a potential increase in domestic terrorism as a result of the conflict. Rep. Wasserman Schultz speaks on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Will Support Supplemental Funding: Rep. Wasserman Schultz

author: Daniel Flatley
description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blasted a JPMorgan Chase & Co. report for what he called “terrible” and inaccurate analysis about constraints over a US government lending agency’s ability to offer backup insurance for oil cargoes attempting to exit the Persian Gulf.
title: Bessent Blasts JPMorgan Over ‘Terrible’ Oil-Insurance Analysis

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump vowed to issue an executive order within one week addressing concerns over athlete salaries, transfers, and the impact of gambling after a session with lawmakers and college sports luminaries that left him frustrated over the prospects for legislation to overhaul college sports.
title: Trump Vows to Issue Order in a Week to Overhaul College Sports

author: Chris Strohm
description: The Justice Department released additional documents related to late, disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein, including FBI interview notes about unverified allegations against Donald Trump.
title: Latest Epstein Release Includes Unverified Claim Against Trump

author: Madison Muller
description: The head of the US Food and Drug Administration’s division of vaccines and gene therapies is leaving the agency after a tumultuous tenure, according to a person familiar with the matter who wasn’t authorized to speak publicly.
title: Top Vaccine Regulator at US FDA Set to Leave Post Next Month

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: White House events continue, though the conflict with Iran is ever-present.
title: Trump Tries to Keep Business-as-Usual Approach Amid War Turmoil

author: Tala Ahmadi
description: Russian President Vladimir Putin emphasized the need for an immediate halt to hostilities in the Middle East during a phone call Friday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, according to the state-run Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting.
title: Putin Urges End to Hostilities in Call With Iran’s Pezeshkian

description: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said interest rates could be on hold for quite some time as inflation comes down and the labor market stabilizes further. She says the economy is in a reasonably good place. She speaks to Bloomberg's Michael McKee in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed's Hammack Sees Two-Sided Risks to Interest Rates

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss today's trade as stocks stay under pressure with oil hitting $90 a barrel and a weak February payrolls report stoking risk-off sentiment. Bloomberg's Mike McKee and LinkedIn Chief Economist Karin Kimbrough weigh in on payrolls. Then, Ellen Wald, President of Transversal Consulting and Senior Fellow at the Atlantic Council, discusses the oil market as the Iran war ignites concerns over fuel supplies and pushes oil prices and US pump prices higher. Plus, Bloomberg News Senior Editor for Credit James Crombie weighs in on more private credit worries as BlackRock curbs withdrawals from one of its biggest private funds. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stocks Lower on $90 Oil, Weak Payrolls | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/6/2026

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall discuss the latest from Iran. On today's show, Former Supreme Allied Commander Europe Wesley Clark, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, former White House Director of Legislative Affairs Marc Short and Groundwork Collaborative Managing Director Liz Pancotti. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Demands Iran Surrender | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/06/2026

author: Lydia Beyoud, Nicola M White
description: Wall Street’s two top regulators are discussing plans to move into the same building complex in Washington just steps from the US Capitol, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Wall Street Regulators Discuss Moving Into Same Building Complex

author: Nancy Cook, Joshua Green
description: The military strikes — and their impact on the economy — have emerged as a grave political vulnerability for Republicans ahead of midterm elections.
title: ‘MAGA Is Split’: Trump’s War in Iran Divides America First Loyalists

author: Will Wade
description: The US energy secretary and a congressman are calling to restart a shuttered nuclear plant north of New York City, saying it’s needed to meet surging demand for power.
title: Energy Secretary Wright Calls to Reopen Indian Point Nuclear Plant

author: Maggie Eastland, Jen Judson
description: Anthropic PBC runs the risk of losing a wide range of US government business after the Defense Department declared it a supply-chain risk, a rare designation that until now has only been assigned to companies from adversary nations like China’s Huawei Technologies Co.
title: Anthropic at Risk of Huawei-Like Ban After Pentagon Punishment

author: Donato Paolo Mancini, Fiona MacDonald, Samy Adghirni
description: Saudi Arabia has stepped up direct engagement with Iran to try and contain a war in the Middle East that is causing havoc and stressing global markets, according to several European officials.
title: Saudi Arabia Has Intensified Direct Line to Iran to Defuse War

author: Laura Dhillon Kane
description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Canada-US Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc met Friday in Washington in the first high-level, in-person talks in months between the two men.
title: Greer, LeBlanc Meet as USMCA Countries Gear Up for Talks

author: Joe Lovinger
description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has spent a year running for the US Senate saying how much he loves Donald Trump. The president just won’t say it back when it matters most.
title: Ken Paxton Vows to Stay in Senate Race No Matter Trump’s Call

author: Marton Eder, Thomas Escritt
description: Ukrainian trucks detained by Hungarian officers carrying about $82 million of gold, euro and dollar bank notes was part of a regular transport to meet cash needs of companies and citizens in the war-torn country, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: $82 Million Stash Held Up by Orban Is Regular Money Transport

author: Erik Larson
description: A US Customs and Border Protection official told a federal judge on Friday that the agency can’t comply with a court order to halt a key step in the tariff payment process after the US Supreme Court struck down the president’s global levies.
title: US Tells Tariff Refund Judge It Can’t Comply With Court Order

author: Patrick Sykes, Dina Esfandiary
description: The killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in US and Israeli strikes have mobilized every branch of Iran’s sprawling state apparatus in a fight for survival.
title: Who’s Who in Iran? Guide to the Islamic Republic’s Power Players

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, James Attwood
description: The Trump administration has opened the door for Venezuela to sell gold into the US in a major boost to a country facing crippling dollar shortages due to restrictions on oil exports.
title: Trump Gives US Gold Buyers a Way Around Venezuelan Sanctions

author: Nacha Cattan
description: As New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s tax-the-rich plans spark backlash among New York’s wealthy, at least one cohort of millionaires is fully supportive of his policies.
title: A Sliver of NYC’s Wealthy Has Unusual Rallying Cry: Tax Me More

author: Olesia Safronova
description: US and Ukrainian negotiators discussed forging a free-trade agreement between their countries as well as a sovereign fund to aid the country’s postwar recovery, according to a top official in Kyiv.
title: US Weighing Ukraine Trade Pact and Recovery Fund, Minister Says

author: Julie Johnsson, Catherine Lucey
description: President Donald Trump is set to host executives from top Pentagon contractors, amid worries around depleting stockpiles as the war on Iran approaches the one-week mark with no clear end in sight.
title: US Says It Has ‘Enough Munitions’ as Trump Summons Defense Firms

description: National Economic Director Kevin Hassett says the White House has no plans to tap the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to bring down oil prices. He says the US nonfarm payrolls report for February, which showed a loss of 92,000 jobs, was an "outlier." He speaks to Jonathan Ferro. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Hassett on Oil Price Pressure, US Jobs Report

author: Arne Delfs
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned the US and Israel against waging an “endless war” against Iran that could lead to the disintegration of the whole Middle Eastern state, a new migration crisis in Europe and lasting economic damage.
title: Merz Warns of Economic Damage Due to ‘Endless’ War Against Iran

author: Iain Marlow, Patrick Sykes
description: President Donald Trump said he doesn’t want to negotiate an end to the war with Iran in a post on social media that demanded Tehran capitulate as US and Israeli airstrikes continue.
title: Trump Wants ‘Unconditional Surrender,’ Won’t Seek Iran Deal

author: Jason Leopold
description: A Department of Justice document combined with interviews reveal that a long-running investigation into organized crime led law enforcement to suspect the serial sex abuser of money laundering, distributing ‘club drugs’ and operating a prostitution ring.
title: Ketamine, Prostitution and Money: Details of a Secret DEA Probe of Jeffrey Epstein

author: Oscar Medina
description: Colombia is at risk of being seduced by populists espousing radical and extreme policies, according to presidential candidate Roy Barreras.
title: Power Broker Barreras Aims to Restore Investor Faith in Colombia

description: Nonfarm payrolls dropped by 92,000, analysts expected a gain of 55,000. The unemployment rate climbed to 4.4%. Bloomberg's Michael McKee reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Unexpectedly Loses 92,000 Jobs in February

author: Galit Altstein
description: The Israel Defense Forces says it’s demolished a majority of Iran’s ballistic-missile launchers, causing the number of missiles targeting Israel and other countries in the region to fall throughout the week.
title: Israel Says It’s Destroyed Most of Iran’s Missile Launchers

author: Patricia Garip, Matthew Malinowski
description: Donald Trump is gathering his top allies from Latin America at a moment when a new US military conflict is putting even his best friends in the region under newfound pressure.
title: Trump’s Latin American Allies Face a Dilemma Over China, Iran War

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright
description: Switzerland plans to buy only about 30 Lockheed Martin Corp. F-35 fighter jets from the US and considers purchasing a European-built air defense system to make up for delays of an existing procurement.
title: Swiss Reduce F-35 Order to 30, Mull European Air Defense System

description: The US-Israeli war has left at least 1,332 people dead in Iran so far, and dozens of others have been killed elsewhere in the region in retaliatory strikes. The Pentagon said six US troops have been killed, all in the first two days of fighting.  President Donald Trump said the US continues to "totally demolish" Iranian forces, telling NBC he wanted to "clean out" Iran's leadership structure and he had names in mind to take over.  Cathy Ashton - who was the EU's first high representative on foreign affairs from 2009-2014, and a key negotiator of the previous Iran nuclear deal known as the JC-POA Stephen Carroll and Lizzy Burden on Bloomberg radio to discuss the conflict and what might come next. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Big Questions Over US Objectives Says Cathy Ashton

author: Andrea Palasciano, Alberto Nardelli
description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa will discuss the unfolding Middle East conflict with Gulf country leaders on Monday, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke on the condition of anonymity.
title: EU’s Von Der Leyen, Costa to Speak With Gulf Leaders Monday

author: Ragnhildur Sigurdardottir
description: Iceland will hold a referendum in August to lay the groundwork for potentially joining the European Union at a later date as the island nation forges a closer relationship with Europe.
title: Iceland to Vote in August on Talks With European Union

author: Swati Gupta
description: The party led by a 35-year-old rapper-turned-politician is leading in national elections in Nepal, putting it on track to break the traditional political establishment’s grip on the Himalayan nation.
title: Nepal’s Pro-Gen Z Party Leads Vote by Wide Margin in Election

author: Andrey Biryukov
description: Iran’s drone and missile strikes targeting Gulf countries in response to US and Israel attacks are rebounding on its own economy.
title: Iran’s Attacks on the UAE Are Costing It Access to Vital Imports

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum was still flying back from Venezuela when the Trump administration made it official: The US would re-establish diplomatic relations with the South American country, seven years after suspending operations at its embassy in Caracas.
title: Trump Woos Venezuela With Potential Deals as Relations Reset

author: Dan Strumpf
description: Strike by US submarine of Iranian vessel near Sri Lanka hurts PM’s position.
title: Modi Feels the Heat From Trump’s War on Iran

author: Patrick Sykes, Grant Smith
description: Israel and Iran exchanged missile fire as the war in the Middle East entered a seventh day, with the impact rippling across global supply chains and energy markets.
title: Iran and Israel Trade Fire as War Impacts Global Supply Chains

description:
"This is a very tough regime...willing to kill to remain in power."

Princeton University Prof. Bernard Haykel tells Mishal Husain why the Iranian regime could survive the war — despite much of the senior leadership being killed in US-Israeli strikes. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why the Iranian Regime Could Survive

author: Zahra Hirji, Lauren Rosenthal
description: The Department of Homeland Security oversees the nation’s main disaster response agency, which has undergone turmoil under Noem.
title: Three Big Questions Facing FEMA With Kristi Noem Out

author: Tracy Alloway, Joe Weisenthal
description: It's more than just oil that's being affected.
title: Lots More on the Seaborne Chaos Around the Strait of Hormuz

author: Tracy Alloway, Joe Weisenthal
description: With war breaking out in Iran, the price of oil is surging, in part due to the destruction of oil energy infrastructure, but also the ability of anything to get through the Strait of Hormuz. But it’s not just oil that moves through this key waterway — there are plenty of other goods, including metals and ingredients for fertilizer getting potentially constrained. It’s also not just the risk of violence itself that’s an issue for shipping companies, there’s also the question of how cargoes get in
title: Lots More on Seaborne Chaos Around the Persian Gulf (Podcast)

author: Swati Gupta, Norman Harsono, Tassia Sipahutar
description: Two of the world’s most populous nations are joining a growing global movement to ban teenagers from social media services.
title: Global Social Media Bans Gain Steam With India, Indonesia

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, the US says it is studying options to arrest a jump in oil prices driven by the Iran conflict. Ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has nearly stopped completely, according to the Joint Maritime Information Center. 

President Trump told NBC he wants to replace Iran’s entire leadership structure and has some names in mind for a “good leader,” declining to elaborate.

Today's guests: King's College London Visiting Fellow Negah Angha & Energy Aspects Global Gas Head Livia Gallarati. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Trump Weighs Range of Options to Counter Oil Price Spike | Daybreak Europe 03/06/2026

author: Jeremy Hodges
description: UK police arrested four men under the National Security Act accused of assisting Iran’s foreign intelligence service.
title: UK Arrests Four Men Accused of Assisting Iranian Spies

author: Milda Seputyte
description: Vladimir Putin is determined to keep spending on strengthening Russia’s military despite a weakening economy, according to a Lithuanian intelligence assessment.
title: Putin to Press On With War Despite Economy Woes, Lithuania Warns

description: A crucial question for how the war will play out is understanding Iran’s missile depth —  its ability to strike US military bases in the Middle East, Israel, and America’s partners in the Gulf. Getting to an answer is tough, as Bloomberg Economics Defense Lead Becca Wasser explains.
title: Calculating Iran’s Missile Math After First Week of War

author: Bilal Hussain
description: Pakistan won’t begin talks to end clashes with Afghanistan until Kabul stops supporting and harboring militant groups that launch cross-border attacks from its territory, a spokesman for Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said.
title: Pakistan Rules Out Talks With Afghanistan as Clashes Continue

description: US President Donald Trump is weighing a range of options for addressing the spike in oil and gasoline prices as the war in the Middle East continues. Trump has spoken with top advisers including Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to discuss the situation. Bloomberg's Stephen Stapczynski reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Weighs Range of Options to Counter Oil Price Spike

author: Yian Lee
description: China hasn’t dispatched a single warplane near Taiwan for the past seven days, a mysterious shift that amounts to Beijing’s longest absence since Taipei started regularly disclosing the activity.
title: China Mysteriously Cuts PLA Flights Into Sensitive Taiwan Areas

author: Piotr Skolimowski, Thomas Escritt
description: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha accused Hungary of unlawfully detaining seven employees of its state-owned Oschadbank in Budapest, the latest in a series of disputes between the neighboring states.
title: Ukraine Accuses Hungary of Seizing Bank Staff in Fresh Spat

description: Middle East scholar Bernard Haykel explains Tehran’s retaliation calculus, the risk of regime collapse and how Saudi Arabia’s crown prince views the Iran war. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What Mohammad bin Salman Fears Most From the Iran War

author: John Harney
description: US Representative Tony Gonzales announced Thursday night that he would not run again, days after the Texas Republican acknowledged an affair with a member of his staff who killed herself.
title: Texas Congressman Gonzales Drops Reelection Bid Amid Scandal

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon
description: The Philippines’ top security official said more people are being probed after authorities apprehended three Filipino nationals for allegedly leaking sensitive information to Beijing, including data on Manila’s operations in the disputed South China Sea.
title: Philippines Probing More Filipinos After Alleged Leak of Sensitive Data to China

description: The US and Israel continue airstrikes on Tehran as President Donald Trump vows to "totally demolish" Iranian forces. Bloomberg’s Patrick Sykes and Dan Williams break down the latest escalation and the potential contenders for the country's leadership. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Conflict Enters Seventh Day With No Reprieve

author: Nectar Gan
description: Former Hong Kong media mogul Jimmy Lai has decided not to appeal his 20-year prison sentence, a move that may cement the pro-democracy activist’s fate behind bars for what could be the remainder of his life.
title: Hong Kong’s Jimmy Lai Decides Against Appealing 20-Year Sentence

author: Swati Pandey
description: Three Australian Defence Force personnel were among the crew of a US submarine that torpedoed and sank an Iranian vessel in the Indian Ocean, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said, while adding that none were involved in operations related to the attack.
title: US Sub That Torpedoed Iranian Ship Included Australians, PM Says

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright, Levin Stamm
description: The Swiss may be about to reaffirm their fondness for cash with a vote that would give the francs in their wallets a place in the constitution.
title: Switzerland’s Voters Are About to Put Cash in the Constitution

author: Andrea Palasciano
description: The European Union’s enlargement chief said the destabilized world requires new rules to accelerate Ukraine’s membership bid, confirming the country won’t be able to join by its 2027 goal under the current process.
title: Top EU Official Wants New Rules to Let Ukraine Join Faster

author: Claire Jiao
description: A 10% increase in energy prices that persists for a year would push global inflation up by 40 basis points and slow economic growth by 0.1-0.2%, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said.
title: IMF Says 10% Oil Rise for Year Adds 40 Basis Points to Inflation

author: Philip Heijmans
description: The US submarine strike on an Iranian warship in the Indian Ocean marked a sharp escalation in the war between the two nations, raising fresh security and economic risks across the Indo-Pacific.
title: US Submarine Strike in Indian Ocean Brings Iran War to Asia

author: Myungshin Cho, Cat Barton
description: South Korea’s Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Seoul is in talks with United States Forces Korea about the possible redeployment of weapons including Patriot air-defense systems, as Washington’s conflict with Iran escalates.
title: Seoul Confirms US Talks on Moving Weapons as Iran War Escalates

author: Myles Miller, Jeff Mason
description: Kristi Noem’s 13-month tenure leading the Department of Homeland Security was marked by controversy. But it wasn’t the two American citizens’ deaths at the hands of federal immigration agents that ultimately cost her the job, nor the allegations of an affair with an adviser, or the criticism that she was slow to provide federal reimbursements to states after natural disasters.
title: ‘As Dead as Fried Chicken’: Why Trump Finally Fired Noem

description: Iranian missiles over central Israel, on March 5. Photographer: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP Photo
title: War Keeps Strait of Hormuz Almost Totally Shut, Raising Energy Prices

author: Swati Pandey, Matthew Brockett
description: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon on Friday moved to quell speculation he’ll resign after a national poll showed sinking public support for his National Party, which he said still stood firmly behind him.
title: New Zealand Premier Luxon Rules Out Resignation After Poll Shock

author: Anusha Ondaatjie
description: Sri Lanka has taken control of an Iranian naval vessel that faced technical problems in its waters, days after a US submarine attack sunk an Iranian warship close to the island.
title: Sri Lanka Comes to Aid of Second Iranian Naval Vessel
